Players destroyed MMOs on multiple levels.

Grifers have always been an issue in MMOs. No matter what you do they'll always find a way... but at the same time the people complaining about grifers also became an issue. We thrive on conflict, and people go so intolerant to grifers that they would call any form of negativity griefing, including playing the game as it was intended in some PvP instances.

Players don't really know what they want and developers are encouraged to give it to them anyway. In the short run this leads to an increase in sales, but over time will lead to a worse game and dwindling community. The things that the players don't even know what they want are always the ones that impress them the most, and usually add the most fun to the game.

Balance/nerfing. This plays off the previous comment. Too much emphasis is put on the players (especially a vocal minority) when it comes to balancing games. From a developer's perspective this is extremely difficult for two reasons... 1.) You play the game so much, usually in specific ways, that it gets hard to know what an average player is like. 2.) You play the game so little in a non-testing way that it's hard to know what the average player is like. I know this sounds impossible, but play testing is so different from actual playing that it tends to build completely different skills. Analytics help in this area a bit, but even with them this is a VERY hard thing to tackle, especially after the initial launch of the game when adding new features. I wish I had more of a solution for this!

Good people get driven away easily, boiling down to communities no one wants to be in. This is partially an issue with the "customer is always right" mentality, and is usually only a real critical-mass problem in games that have been around for a while. As time goes on it becomes difficult for new people to fit in. It's sad, but a lot of the nicer more friendly and helpful people get worn down and bitter over time. No, I'm not saying everyone... but usually in a late-life game this is something that's a rare site. Yes, this relates to the griefer problem, but it's not just that. Niches form. Bonds are made. Hardcore players are much more likely to stay the long road than average, and they often feel more unapproachable, even if they're nice.

These are just a few observations I've made over the past 20+ years of playing MMOs and 8ish years of running one. I hope someone found this interesting!
